subject: general
question: Cyclohexane is best classified as which type of organic compound?

options.text: A branched hydrocarbon with one or more unsaturated carbon bonds
An aromatic compound containing a delocalised pi -electron ring system
An organic aldehyde consisting of a linear chain of six carbon atoms
A saturated alicyclic compound composed of six carbon atoms in a ring

solution:
The correct answer is __**A saturated alicyclic compound composed of six carbon atoms in a ring**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cyclohexane** is a **cycloalkane** with the molecular formula **C6H12**. It consists of **six carbon atoms** arranged in a ring, with each carbon atom bonded to **two hydrogen atoms**.
 
• The term **saturated** indicates that all the **carbon-carbon bonds** in the molecule are **single bonds**, and it contains the maximum possible number of hydrogen atoms for its cyclic structure. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• It is classified as an **alicyclic** compound because it is both **aliphatic** (non-aromatic) and **cyclic**. It does not possess a **linear chain** of atoms. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Unlike **benzene**, cyclohexane does not have a **delocalised π-electron ring system** and is not **aromatic**. Each carbon in cyclohexane is **sp3 hybridized**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Cyclohexane is a simple ring structure and is not classified as a **branched hydrocarbon**, nor does it contain **unsaturated** double or triple bonds. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure and Conformations**: 
 
 
• Due to the **tetrahedral** bond angles of **sp3 hybridized** carbon, cyclohexane is not a planar molecule. It adopts various **conformations** to minimize **torsional strain** and **angle strain**.
 
• The most stable arrangement is the **chair conformation**, followed by the **twist-boat**, **boat**, and **half-chair** conformations.
 
 
 
• **Physical Properties**: 
 
 
• Cyclohexane is a **colorless**, flammable liquid at room temperature with a **detergent-like odor**. 
 
• It has a **molar mass** of approximately **84.16 g/mol**, a **density** of **0.779 g/cm³**, and a **boiling point** of **80.7 °C**.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Production and Uses**: 
 
 
• On a large scale, it is produced by the **hydrogenation of benzene** in the presence of a **nickel** or **platinum** catalyst.
 
• It serves as a critical **intermediate** in the production of **nylon**. Specifically, it is oxidized to produce **cyclohexanone** and **cyclohexanol**, which are then used to manufacture **adipic acid** and **caprolactam**.
 
• It is also widely used as a **non-polar solvent** in chemical laboratories and industrial processes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Alicyclic vs Aromatic**: 
 
 
• **Alicyclic compounds** (like cyclohexane) behave more like **open-chain aliphatic** compounds in their chemical reactions, such as **free radical substitution**.
 
• **Aromatic compounds** (like **benzene**, **C6H6**) follow **Huckel's Rule** (**4n + 2 π electrons**) and undergo **electrophilic aromatic substitution** rather than addition.
 
 
 
• **Hybridization**: In cyclohexane, every carbon atom uses **four sp3 hybrid orbitals** to form **sigma (σ) bonds**, resulting in a bond angle of approximately **109.5°**.
 
• **Cycloalkanes General Formula**: The general formula for a monocyclic cycloalkane like cyclohexane is **CnH2n**, which differs from the open-chain alkane formula **CnH2n+2** because of the ring closure.
